newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IMF bullish on Argentina, but warns about deficit.
newsitem.headline: IMF bullish on Argentina, but warns about deficit.

text.p: The IMF has issued a bullish assessment of Argentina's economic fundamentals in a confidential report but predicts the government this year will exceed a budget deficit target it agreed with the fund.
The report, obtained by Reuters, was dated July 16 and followed a visit by an International Monetary Fund team in May to review a standby deal with the fund reached last year.
The IMF highlighted the economy was growing rapidly, inflation was nearly zero and Argentina was less vulnerable to external shocks than after the 1994 Mexican peso devaluation.

The IMF said it projected lower value-added tax revenue and higher social security spending than did the government. Social security benefits in the first quarter were four percent above the forecast amount due to unexpected claims for retroactive court-mandated payments to retirees.

"The staff recommended therefore that early corrective measures be taken as a pro-active signal of the authorities' resolve to meet the agreed targets and to provide a safety margin for the rest of the year," the report said.

Argentine officials explained to them there was limited scope for increasing taxes in the short term since this would require legislative approval, "and such approval was unlikely to materialize in the run up to the elections."
The ruling Peronist party has begun campaigning heavily to maintain a parliamentary majority in midterm polls in October.
Fiscal targets agreed with the fund were met for the first half of 1997 and Argentine officials insist they will remain within their yearly goal of $3 billion, or 0.9 percent of GDP.
"The (IMF) staff commended the authorities for their management of the program so far," the report said. "Expenditure restraint had played a key role."

However, "on the fiscal outlook for the remainder of the year, staff projections were slightly less favorable than those of the authorities, with a projected deviation from the annual deficit target of around $0.5 billion."
